# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb currently shows display `0`, a blue light, a large button marked `PUSH TO DEFUSE`, and three wires: green, yellow, red. I am sending the complete visual state to Mute, who can consult the manual and relay the required action to Blind. I cannot interpret the gestures as spoken information, so Mute should use speech for the manual’s instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state: display 0; light blue; large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Please consult the manual and speak the exact required procedure to Blind, including whether to press the button or cut a wire and which one.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I still do not know what the manual requires, because Mute’s gestures are not a reliable substitute for their spoken message, and I cannot hear speech. I will ensure Blind has the complete visual information and direct Blind to follow Mute’s manual-based instruction rather than infer an action from my description.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state remains: display 0, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Follow Mute's spoken manual instruction for the exact safe action; do not act from this description alone.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The visual state is unchanged, and I still have no confirmed manual instruction. I am establishing a simple reporting code with Blind: Blind can hear my speech and can gesture back for me to see. Blind must not manipulate the bomb until Mute has supplied the exact manual-based procedure.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Use gestures to report status to me: gesture 👍 if Mute has given you an exact safe procedure from the manual; gesture 👎 if not. Do not operate the bomb unless the procedure is exact.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind now. Blind will report to me with gesture thumbs up only after receiving a complete safe instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:

BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Blind reports that no exact safe procedure has been received. I am reinforcing the request to Mute through both available channels: Mute should read the manual and state the complete procedure aloud to Blind, rather than use gestures or assume that the label alone determines the action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind reports no exact procedure received. Read the manual now and speak the complete safe procedure aloud to Blind: identify the required control, any timing or display condition, and the exact action. Do not gesture the answer.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🫵"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s gestures do not convey the manual’s procedure to me, and Blind has not yet reported a confirmed instruction. I am asking Blind to report whether Mute has now spoken a complete procedure; no bomb action should be taken without that confirmation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Has Mute now spoken the complete manual procedure to you? Gesture 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. If yes, do not act yet unless the procedure is unambiguous.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot hear speech. Please speak the exact manual procedure aloud to Blind, including the specific control and any conditions; do not rely on gestures.")
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Blind still signals that no complete procedure has reached them. The bomb remains unchanged, so no action has been accepted or attempted. Mute must use speech—not gestures—to relay the manual’s exact instruction to Blind, who should then confirm with a thumbs-up gesture before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind still reports no procedure. You are the only one who can read the manual and speak its answer. Speak the exact complete instruction aloud to Blind now, including the control, wire or button, and every condition. Do not use gestures.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👎", "🫵"])
```

WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝]

The bomb’s state is still unchanged. We have not yet established a usable code, so Mute’s three gestures cannot safely be interpreted as the manual’s answer. I am now defining a compact code: Mute will report whether the manual requires pressing the button or cutting a wire, and if cutting, which wire. I will then relay that result by speech to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact gesture code for the manual answer: first gesture 👍 means press the button; first gesture 👎 means cut a wire. If cutting, second gesture ☝ means wire 1 green, ✌ means wire 2 yellow, and 🤟 means wire 3 red. Send only the required answer in this format. Do not act.")
speak(to="blind", text="We are establishing a code with Mute. Do not touch the bomb yet. I will relay the manual answer by speech once Mute reports it.")
```

WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]

Mute has reported `👎 ☝`, which under the agreed code means the manual requires cutting a wire, specifically wire 1, the green wire. I am relaying that exact instruction to Blind, who can perform the physical action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual answer received: cut wire 1, the green wire. Do not press the button.")
```
